Subject: Hosted API pricing — commit playbook & next steps

Hi Sara / Tom,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through Avery's planned usage patterns. Quick recap and a proposed playbook so we can get a formal quote over to procurement. Please reply with any corrections.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Expected steady-state monthly consumption: 30M–50M tokens (month 1 baseline ~30M, ramping to ~45M over 90 days).
- Peak TPS observed in demo: ~120 TPS; expected peak windows for production: 120–160 TPS (10–60s bursts).
- Target budget: mid-range $15–$25 per 1M tokens depending on commitment and SLA.

Redwood hosted pricing options (high-level guidance):
- No commit (on-demand): list rate ~ $30 / 1M tokens (good for pilots).
- Committed slabs (recommended for material savings):
  • 10M–49M / month -> ~$22 / 1M
  • 50M–199M / month -> ~$17 / 1M
- Burst/peak handling: hosted supports short bursts above reserved concurrency; we recommend a modest reserve capacity + burst credits for predictable 99th percentile latency.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm the expected monthly band you want priced for the first 3 months (choose one: 30M, 45M, 60M)?
2) Confirm whether Avery needs a hard SLA (99.9% uptime + latency SLO) — this affects pricing and reserved capacity sizing.
3) If confirmed, we will send two quote flavors: (A) 6-month commit at the 50M slab pricing and (B) 3-month flexible slab at 30–45M.

I'm attaching a short pricing worksheet with example math to illustrate per-1M economics and overall monthly spend.

Availability to review the formal quote: I have availability Mon 14 Sep 10:00–11:00 PT or Tue 15 Sep 08:00–09:00 PT — which works for you?

Thanks — looking forward to locking down numbers and getting a proposal out.

Best,
Karthik Iyer

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. All looks right from our side with two clarifications:

1) Monthly volume: conservative baseline 30M for first month, plan to be ~45M by month 3 and potentially 70–80M by Q1 if the pilot succeeds. For the initial contract we want pricing for both a 30M and a 50M committed scenario so we can compare.
2) Peak TPS: 120 TPS typical peak; we have a couple of short jobs that could hit 160 TPS for 20–30s; reliability is more important than absolute sustained QPS — so the SLA/latency SLO is relevant.

Budget band: we are aiming for total platform spend in the $14k–$40k / month range depending on unit price (targeting $15–$22 per 1M ideally).

Please send a formal quote showing: committed-tier pricing, expected monthly cost math, any one-time setup or dedicated capacity fees, and how burst/capacity credits are charged.

We can do Mon 14 Sep 10:00 PT for a quick call — locking it in on my calendar now.

Thanks — Sara

Sara — perfect, thanks for the confirmations. Per your ask, I'll send a formal quote; below is the playbook we will include in the proposal and what impacts unit economics.

Proposal summary (what we'll deliver Monday):
- Quote A (50M committed / month, 6-month term): unit price $17 / 1M, includes reserved concurrency to meet 99.9% uptime and a burst buffer sized for 200 TPS short bursts. One-time onboarding fee: $5k (covers private onboarding and SRE runbook).
- Quote B (30M committed / month, 3-month term): unit price $22 / 1M, smaller reserved pool, burst credits billed separately if used > agreed buffer. No onboarding discount.

Example math (month 1):
- 30M @ $22 = $660.00 *note: we use per-1M units in billing; total invoice = $660 (this is illustrative).
- 50M @ $17 = $850.00
(we will include full line-item math and token accounting details in the quote; see attached PDF for scenario comparison)

Operational notes:
- Peak TPS: we'll size a modest reserve to cover typical 120 TPS peaks; recommended 50M slab gives better headroom for unexpected spikes and materially lowers $/1M.
- Billing: monthly invoiced; overage rules and burst credits spelled out.

Attachments enclosed for Monday: redwood-hosted-pricing-sheet-AVY.xlsx, redwood-commit-scenarios-AVY.pdf. I'll upload a draft DocuSign quote to the link below before our call so your procurement team can speed review.

Preserving the Monday 14 Sep 10:00 PT slot — Zoom invite and draft quote will be in your calendar invite shortly.
